proposal: The Mandate recommends that DOL prohibit ERISA plan investing based on factors unrelated to investor risk and return and return to the first Trump Administration's approach of permitting only pecuniary factors, while still allowing legitimate non-ESG factors such as governance or domestic supply chains. It also suggests considering greater scrutiny of plan investments in China.

status_summary: DOL has announced a replacement rulemaking but had not published a proposal as of 2026-10-07. On 2025-04-21 DOL told the Fifth Circuit it would reconsider the 2022 investment-duties rule (which allows ESG factors as tiebreakers), and on 2025-05-28 it said it would pursue new rulemaking on the same subject. The federal regulatory agenda lists the rulemaking as RIN 1210-AC37, Prudence and Loyalty in Selecting Plan Investments and Exercising Shareholder Rights, an economically significant rule that would revise 29 CFR 2550.404a-1 so fiduciaries choose investments and vote shares based only on financial considerations; the agenda edition read at reginfo.gov lists a proposed-rule date of July 2026, which passed without a Federal Register notice. The 2022 rule therefore remains in effect, and DOL's separate 2026-03-31 proposal on selecting investment alternatives (alternative assets) does not address ESG.

timeline.event: In the Fifth Circuit appeal over the 2022 rule (Utah v. Chavez-DeRemer, formerly Utah v. Walsh), DOL asks to hold the case in abeyance, saying it intends to reconsider the rule, including whether to rescind it; the court grants only a 30-day pause on 2025-04-28.
DOL tells the Fifth Circuit it will engage in new rulemaking on the subject of the challenged 2022 rule, to appear in the spring regulatory agenda.

Adjacent action, not on ESG: DOL's Employee Benefits Security Administration proposes a regulation and safe harbor on the duty of prudence in choosing designated investment alternatives, including funds with alternative assets, implementing Executive Order 14330; comments closed 2026-06-01. The portions read did not discuss ESG or the 2022 rule.

Target month (month only; first of month used) for the proposed rule on prudence and loyalty in selecting plan investments in the regulatory agenda entry RIN 1210-AC37 as shown at reginfo.gov; no proposal appears in the Federal Register through 2026-10-07.

The Federal Register publishes the introduction to the 2026 Unified Agenda, which includes the DOL entry titled Prudence and Loyalty in Selecting Plan Investments and Exercising Shareholder Rights at the proposed-rule stage.

The agenda abstract describes the content in general terms only; the Mandate's allowance for legitimate non-ESG factors and its China-scrutiny recommendation are not addressed in it.
